justification: The repository exhibits strong modularity in its directory structure but suffers from insufficient *behavioral* decomposition: multiple high-impact modules (e.g., mmseg.models.decode_heads.decode_head, mmseg.datasets.custom, mmseg.datasets.builder) contain deeply nested conditionals, mixed concerns (training, inference, logging, evaluation), and multi-thousand-line files (e.g., train.py, test.py, custom.py). Static analysis confirms high cognitive complexity (factors include 'T4' and 'A1'). This violates maintainability principles because testability and analyzability require that each module perform a single, well-defined responsibility—currently violated in pipeline composition, dataset handling, and model building logic. The solution is to apply Decomposability: break monolithic modules into smaller, purpose-specific units without changing the registry-based extensibility, directly improving testability and reducing ripple effects during change.
expected_architectural_change: Monolithic core modules (custom.py, builder.py, decode_head.py) will be split into focused, single-responsibility components (e.g., DatasetLoader, AnnotationValidator, AnnotationPreprocessor, EvaluationPlanner) while preserving the existing registry abstraction boundaries. Pipeline composition will shift from a linear Compose loop to a chain of composable decorators or strategies. The public APIs remain unchanged, but internal coupling between dataset loading, transform application, evaluation, and logging will be reduced, increasing cohesion within each unit.
implementation_strategy: 1. Identify responsibilities within mmseg/datasets/custom.py: load_annotations, prepare_train_img, format_results, evaluate—each becomes a separate interface/abstract base. 2. Extract annotation loading and preprocessing into dedicated classes implementing a unified interface. 3. Refactor builder.py to delegate dataset assembly to role-specific builders (LoaderBuilder, TransformBuilder, EvaluatorBuilder) instead of one monolithic build_dataset. 4. Split train.py/test.py logic into orchestrators that compose these smaller components. 5. Introduce explicit interfaces (e.g., EvaluationPlanner, MetricAggregator) to replace inline conditional metric computation. All changes preserve the Registry's role and API signatures.
risks: Low: Changes are additive and testable incrementally (e.g., one dataset pipeline step at a time). Risk of temporary duplication during refactoring is mitigated by the existing extensive test suite (mmseg/datasets/test_*.py), allowing safe refactoring with continuous validation. No new deployment or runtime dependencies introduced; purely internal refactoring.
